data.standardized_narrative: The syndicate's opening gross claims outstanding at 1 January 2023 was $53.078m. Analysis of the gross claims development table shows a net adverse movement on prior underwriting years (predominantly the 2021 underwriting year) of approximately $5.647m (c.10.6% of opening reserves), reflecting strengthening of reserves. The report highlights uncertainty from claims development, inflationary pressures and cyber risk as underlying factors, but does not provide an explicit gross prior-year movement narrative elsewhere.
raw_causal_phrases: The provision for claims outstanding comprises the estimated cost of settling all claims incurred but unpaid at the balance sheet date, whether reported or not.

The rapidly changing environment in the cyber class of business has a higher degree of uncertainty due to the propensity for changes to the cyber risk landscape and perils, such as ransomware emerging in the past couple of years.
Loss estimates are heavily influenced by expected loss ratios on which there is a high level of uncertainty.

There are a number of factors which impact the inflationary environment; such as government or central bank actions, movements in exchange rates impacting the cost of imports, and geopolitical factors such as those already noted above.

gross_premium_mix.line_of_business: Fire and other damage to property

data.data_quality_notes: No explicit gross 'movement in prior year's provision for claims outstanding' note was found. Prior-year development has been calculated from the gross claims development table (cumulative gross claims incurred) by comparing the latest estimate to the prior diagonal for underwriting years excluding the two most recent (only the 2021 underwriting year was available for such a comparison). Amounts in the file are presented in the report's native currency (USD, figures in the accounts are shown in $'000). exact_reserve_text is blank because the report does not provide a standalone sentence explicitly describing the gross prior-year reserve movement. The prior year movement is therefore derived from the triangle (fallback method).
